intro: Myles doesn't hand kids a generic program. He reviews their game film, finds the one thing holding a pitcher back, and fixes it rep by rep — then builds a full arsenal on top of it. Calm, accountable, built from the ground up.

arsenal.name: Fastball
arsenal.blurb: The foundation — built from the legs and forward, no wasted motion. Command it middle-middle, then expand.

arsenal.name: Two-Seam
arsenal.blurb: Over-gripped for heavier run. Thrown over the top so it moves late and hard.

arsenal.name: Changeup
arsenal.blurb: Identical arm action to the fastball, so the hitter can't read it. Death to lower-half hitters.

arsenal.name: Cutter
arsenal.blurb: Thrown like a fastball, breaks late off the natural run. The strikeout pitch.

arsenal.name: Knuckle Curve
arsenal.blurb: Thrown like a football for tumble, dropped right into the zone for a called strike.

method.title: Film first
method.blurb: Every fix starts from real game footage — find the one flaw, then drill it.

method.title: Mechanics that repeat
method.blurb: Squared hips, elbow up, balanced delivery — so it holds up under pressure.

method.title: Game-rep bullpens
method.blurb: Sessions mirror a real outing: establish the fastball, work away, run the secondaries, finish on a heater.

method.title: Accountability
method.blurb: Constant feedback and a standard of focus — tough when it needs to be, encouraging every good rep.
